Colors for the groups compared in an outcome figure

Source: R/palette-hv.R
hv_group_palette.Rd

The house colors for the groups of a survival, hazard or other outcome curve, named by group so each group keeps its color in every figure of a paper. A single group is black. Two to five groups take Paul Tol's vibrant palette, led by red and blue: red #CC3311, blue #0077BB, teal #009988, magenta #EE3377, cyan #33BBEE.

Usage

hv_group_palette(levels)

Arguments

levels

Character vector of distinct group names, in drawing order.

Value

A character vector of hex colors, named by levels and in the same order, for ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = ).

Details

Red and blue mean the event and censored only in a figure that draws those roles, which is hv_role_palette()'s job. In an outcome curve the colors stand for groups, so the strongest two go to the first two groups: they stay apart for a reader with deuteranopia or protanopia (CIELAB distance 104 and 84 under colorspace::deutan() and protan()), and they are hues the team's JTCVS working palette names.

Six or seven groups all switch to Paul Tol's muted palette less sand and cyan, the overflow hv_role_palette() uses. Beyond seven there are no more colorblind-safe colors, and the function stops with an error of class hv_group_palette_capacity.

Pass every level of the grouping factor, not only those a figure draws, so that a figure missing one group does not shift the colors of the rest.

See also

hv_role_palette() for figures whose levels are the event, censored or missing; hv_palette() for categorical groups that are not compared as outcomes.

Examples

hv_group_palette("All")
#>       All 
#> "#000000" 
hv_group_palette(c("Sternotomy", "Robotic", "Thoracotomy"))
#>  Sternotomy     Robotic Thoracotomy 
#>   "#CC3311"   "#0077BB"   "#009988"
